title: Ecosystems in the Philippines
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Ecosystems in the Philippines Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The Philippines has many ecosystems: tropical rainforests, mossy forests, grasslands, mangroves, coral reefs, seagrass beds, lakes, rivers and agricultural ecosystems; human activities affect them; sustainable practices protect them. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 3: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Life Science): forests, mangroves, coral reefs and seagrass, freshwater ecosystems, human impact and sustainability. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Each ecosystem has its own living and non-living parts.
key_sub: Mangroves and coral reefs protect coasts.
body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem is a community of organisms living together with the non-living parts of their environment. Philippine ecosystems include tropical rainforests, mossy forests on high mountains, grasslands, mangrove forests, coral reefs such as Tubbataha, seagrass beds, lakes such as Laguna de Bay, and rice terraces.

Human activities such as logging, blast fishing, pollution and converting mangroves to fishponds damage ecosystems. Marine protected areas, reforestation, waste management and sustainable fishing protect them for future generations.

Example

Which ecosystem grows where the sea meets the land?

Salty water roots

Answer: a mangrove forest

Example

What causes coral bleaching?

Temperature

Answer: warm water makes corals lose their algae

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mangroves are useless swamps.
  • Thinking coral is a plant.
  • Thinking one ecosystem does not affect others.

faq.q: What is a marine protected area?
faq.a: A part of the sea where fishing is limited so fish and corals can recover.
Forests in watersheds keep rivers flowing and reduce floods and landslides.

items.q: Which protected reef in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
items.e: It has a very high diversity of marine life.

items.q: A glacier melts back and leaves bare rock. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

items.q: Which human activity harms coral reefs?
items.e: Blasts and poison destroy corals.

items.q: A remora fish attaches to a shark and eats scraps of its food; the shark is not affected. What is this relationship?
items.e: One benefits, the other is unaffected.

items.q: A forest fire burns trees but leaves the soil. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

items.q: What is a tropical rainforest?
c: a cold forest of pine trees only
a warm, wet forest with tall trees and very high biodiversity
items.e: Philippine rainforests are home to the Philippine eagle.

items.q: Why are coral reefs important?
c: they are home to many fish and protect coasts from waves
they are made of plants only
items.e: The Tubbataha Reefs are a protected marine park.

items.q: Reef-building corals and the algae (zooxanthellae) in their tissues both benefit. What is this relationship?
items.e: The algae give sugars; the coral gives shelter and nutrients.

items.q: Which is a freshwater ecosystem?
c: a mangrove forest by the sea
items.e: Lakes and rivers are freshwater ecosystems.

items.q: A tick feeds on the blood of a bandicoot. What is this relationship?
items.e: The parasite benefits and the host is harmed.

items.q: A population of 360 Philippine deer has 46 births, 13 immigrants, 31 deaths and 19 emigrants in a year. What is the population at the end of the year?
items.e: Nt+1 = Nt + (B + I) − (D + E) = 369.

items.q: What is a seagrass bed?
c: an underwater meadow of flowering plants in shallow seas, where dugongs and fish feed
items.e: Seagrass also traps sediment and stores carbon.

items.q: What is the carrying capacity of an environment?
c: the number of species it contains
the fastest rate at which a population can grow
the largest population it can support for a long time
items.e: Limited by food, water, space and other resources.

items.q: What is primary succession?
c: regrowth of a forest after a bushfire
colonization of bare rock or new land where there was no soil
the arrival of predators in a new area
items.e: Lichens and mosses are pioneer species.

items.q: Why are mangroves called nurseries of the sea?
c: young fish, crabs and shrimp grow up safely among their roots
they grow in the open ocean
items.e: Mangrove roots give shelter.

items.q: Which factor is density-independent?
c: predation that increases with prey numbers
disease spreading through a crowded colony
items.e: Drought affects a population whatever its density.

items.q: Loggers clear a forest, and shrubs grow back. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

items.q: Which Philippine ecosystem has trees whose roots grow in salty water along the coast?
items.e: Mangroves grow between land and sea.

items.q: What is an ecological niche?
c: the food chain a species belongs to
the role of a species, including what it eats, where it lives and how it interacts with others
the place where a species lives only
the number of individuals of a species
items.e: The habitat is only part of the niche.

items.q: Which interaction is shown when a lyrebird and a bandicoot both dig in the leaf litter for the same insects?
items.e: Two species use the same limited resource.

items.q: Burmese pythons spread through the Everglades. Which solution best fits this problem?
c: reduce runoff and waste with buffers and better treatment
set catch limits and protected areas
remove the invaders and check boats and cargo
items.e: Match the solution to the cause.

items.q: Which is a way to protect Philippine ecosystems?
c: planting native trees and mangroves and not throwing garbage in rivers
items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: A new road splits a forest in two. Which human impact is this?
items.e: Name the threat to biodiversity.

items.q: Why should forests on mountains be protected?
c: they hold soil, prevent landslides and keep water in watersheds
items.e: Watersheds supply water to towns.

items.q: Why are wetlands important?
c: they filter water, hold floodwater and are habitats for birds and fish
items.e: The Olango Island wetlands host migratory birds.

items.q: Why are the Philippines called a megadiverse country?
c: it has a very large number of species, many found nowhere else
items.e: Many species are endemic to the Philippine islands.

items.q: Fertilizer runoff causes algae blooms in a lake. Which solution best fits this problem?
c: set catch limits and protected areas
reduce runoff and waste with buffers and better treatment
items.e: Match the solution to the cause.

items.q: Plastic waste collects in the ocean. Which human impact is this?
items.e: Name the threat to biodiversity.

items.q: What is coral bleaching?
c: corals turn white when warm water makes them lose their algae
items.e: Bleached corals may die if the water stays warm.

items.q: Warmer oceans bleach coral reefs. Which human impact is this?
items.e: Name the threat to biodiversity.

items.q: Kenneth learns that marshes soak up floodwater. Which ecosystem service is this?
items.e: Ecosystem services are benefits people get from healthy ecosystems.

items.q: What happens to an ecosystem when one species disappears?
c: the food web changes and other species may be affected
the ecosystem becomes a desert at once
items.e: Living things depend on one another.

items.q: A wetland is drained to build houses. Which solution best fits this problem?
c: reduce runoff and waste with buffers and better treatment
items.e: Match the solution to the cause.

items.q: Which ecosystem is found at the top of high mountains like Mount Pulag?
items.e: It is cooler and wetter high in the mountains.

items.q: Jasmine learns that forests take in carbon dioxide. Which ecosystem service is this?
items.e: Ecosystem services are benefits people get from healthy ecosystems.

items.q: Which ecosystem forms the famous rice terraces of Ifugao?
c: an agricultural ecosystem carved into mountain slopes
items.e: The terraces are fed by water from mountain forests.

items.q: Lava cools into new bare rock. Lichens grow first. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

items.q: Joy learns that tree roots hold soil on hillsides. Which ecosystem service is this?
items.e: Ecosystem services are benefits people get from healthy ecosystems.

items.q: Dennis learns that decomposers break down dead leaves. Which ecosystem service is this?
items.e: Ecosystem services are benefits people get from healthy ecosystems.

A population of 780 Philippine deer has 53 births, 20 immigrants, 5 deaths and 30 emigrants in a year. What is the population at the end of the year?
items.e: Nt+1 = Nt + (B + I) − (D + E) = 818.

items.q: What is carrying capacity (K)?
c: the largest population a habitat can support
items.e: Logistic growth: dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K.

items.q: Producers in a food chain fix 2,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
items.e: Only about 10% passes to each level: 2,000 × 0.12 = 20.0 J.

items.q: What is a trophic level?
c: a feeding position in a food chain
the number of organisms in a habitat
items.e: Producers are level 1, herbivores level 2.

items.q: A population of 880 grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of increase r = 0.200 per year. What is its rate of growth (dN/dt) now?
items.e: dN/dt = rN = 0.200 × 880 = 176 per year.

items.q: A population of 400 grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of increase r = 0.0100 per year. What is its rate of growth (dN/dt) now?
Two species of honeyeater feed on the same flowers. What is this?
items.e: Competition between different species.

items.q: A population of 500 grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of increase r = 0.100 per year. What is its rate of growth (dN/dt) now?
Producers in a food chain fix 8,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
items.e: Only about 10% passes to each level: 8,000 × 0.12 = 80.0 J.

items.q: Clownfish shelter in sea anemones and keep them clean; the anemone's stinging cells protect the fish. What is this relationship?
items.e: Both species benefit.

items.q: A population of 840 Philippine deer has 78 births, 17 immigrants, 20 deaths and 8 emigrants in a year. What is the population at the end of the year?
items.e: Nt+1 = Nt + (B + I) − (D + E) = 907.

items.q: Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five links?
c: there is too much biomass at the top
too little energy is left at the top to support another level
plants cannot support more than one consumer
items.e: Energy decreases at each trophic level.

items.q: A population of 600 Philippine deer has 70 births, 8 immigrants, 21 deaths and 24 emigrants in a year. What is the population at the end of the year?
items.e: Nt+1 = Nt + (B + I) − (D + E) = 633.

items.q: A population of 420 grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of increase r = 0.0200 per year. What is its rate of growth (dN/dt) now?
What is a pioneer species?
c: the first organism to colonize bare ground, such as lichen
the largest tree in a forest
items.e: Pioneers start to form soil.

items.q: A population of 600 grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of increase r = 0.0150 per year. What is its rate of growth (dN/dt) now?
What is secondary succession?
c: regrowth of a community where soil remains after a disturbance such as fire
a food chain with two consumers
items.e: It is faster because soil and seeds are already there.

items.q: Mistletoe takes water and minerals from a eucalyptus. What is the mistletoe?
items.e: Mistletoes are partial parasites of trees.

items.q: Why do people get altitude sickness at high places?
c: the low atmospheric pressure means the body gets less oxygen
items.e: The body adapts by making more red blood cells.

items.q: Producers in a food chain fix 20,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the tertiary consumers?
items.e: Only about 10% passes to each level: 20,000 × 0.13 = 20.0 J.

items.q: Emmanuel's class studies this problem: “Cars and factories burn fossil fuels.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: rain gardens and permeable sidewalk that soak up runoff
planting grass buffer strips along the river and using less fertilizer
cooling the water in ponds before it is released
public transit, electric vehicles and cleaner power
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: Emmanuel reads: “Hunters remove most of the sea otters from a coast.” Is this a change to a physical (nonliving) or biological (living) part of the ecosystem?
items.e: Physical parts include water, soil, temperature and fire; biological parts are living things.

items.q: Diane's class studies this problem: “Plastic bags blow into the ocean.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: reusable bags and bans on single-use plastic
keeping protected green spaces and wildlife corridors
public transit, electric vehicles and cleaner power
rain gardens and permeable sidewalk that soak up runoff
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: Kristine wants to know whether a wildlife bridge reduces animal deaths. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: ask one neighbor what they think
count animals hit on the road before and after the bridge
check once on a single day
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Kevin reads: “Wolves are returned to a national park.” Is this a change to a physical (nonliving) or biological (living) part of the ecosystem?
items.e: Physical parts include water, soil, temperature and fire; biological parts are living things.

items.q: Bryan reads: “A long drought dries up streams.” Is this a change to a physical (nonliving) or biological (living) part of the ecosystem?
items.e: Physical parts include water, soil, temperature and fire; biological parts are living things.

items.q: Ramon observes: “Forests are cleared for new houses.” What impact can this have?
c: warmer water with less oxygen for fish
air pollution and more carbon dioxide
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Angelo observes: “Cars and factories burn fossil fuels.” What impact can this have?
c: warmer water with less oxygen for fish
animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
air pollution and more carbon dioxide
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Vincent observes: “Plastic bags blow into the ocean.” What impact can this have?
c: animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
warmer water with less oxygen for fish
algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Christian's class studies this problem: “Rainwater carries oil and garbage from car parks into streams.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: planting grass buffer strips along the river and using less fertilizer
keeping protected green spaces and wildlife corridors
rain gardens and permeable sidewalk that soak up runoff
public transit, electric vehicles and cleaner power
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: Diane's class studies this problem: “A factory releases hot water into a lake.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: keeping protected green spaces and wildlife corridors
rain gardens and permeable sidewalk that soak up runoff
reusable bags and bans on single-use plastic
cooling the water in ponds before it is released
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: Camille wants to know whether fewer fish die after a farm uses less fertilizer. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: ask one neighbor what they think
count fish and measure oxygen in the river over several years
check once on a single day
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Kristine reads: “A flood covers a river valley with mud.” Is this a change to a physical (nonliving) or biological (living) part of the ecosystem?
items.e: Physical parts include water, soil, temperature and fire; biological parts are living things.

items.q: Gabriel wants to know whether a recycling program reduces garbage. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: weigh the garbage sent to the landfill each week before and after
check once on a single day
ask one neighbor what they think
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Lance learns: Wolves returned to Yellowstone. What happened to the elk?
c: They decreased, and willow trees along rivers grew back.
items.e: A change to one part of an ecosystem affects other populations.

items.q: Diane learns: A drought dried a pond. What happened to the frogs?
c: They moved into the trees permanently.
They decreased because they lost water and food.
items.e: A change to one part of an ecosystem affects other populations.

items.q: Arnel learns: A disease killed many bats. What happened to the night-flying insects?
c: They increased because fewer bats ate them.
items.e: A change to one part of an ecosystem affects other populations.

items.q: Nico wants to know whether a new bus line reduces air pollution. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: ask one neighbor what they think
measure air quality and traffic for several months before and after
check once on a single day
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Jomar wants to know whether a rain garden reduces stream pollution. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: check once on a single day
ask one neighbor what they think
measure pollution in the stream before and after the rain garden is built
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Hazel learns: Sea otters were overhunted. What happened to the sea urchins?
c: They increased and ate the kelp forests.
items.e: A change to one part of an ecosystem affects other populations.

items.q: Why does growing beans, peas or clover help the next crop?
c: bacteria in their roots fix nitrogen, which fertilizes the soil
they make the soil more acidic for good
they remove all water from the soil
they block all sunlight from weeds
items.e: Legumes reduce the need for synthetic fertilizer.

items.q: Jenny's class studies this problem: “A fish population is shrinking from overfishing.” Which solution would best protect biodiversity?
c: set catch limits and protected zones
items.e: It solves the cause of the problem while protecting species.

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: fertilizer runoff causing dead zones?
c: cover crops and buffer strips of plants
items.e: Engineers design solutions that reduce harm to natural systems.

items.q: What is crop rotation?
c: growing different crops in a field in different years
growing the same crop every year
items.e: Rotation keeps soil healthy, breaks pest cycles and can add nitrogen (with legumes such as beans).

items.q: Rose's class studies this problem: “Bee populations are falling near farms.” Which solution would best protect biodiversity?
c: plant wildflower strips and reduce pesticide use
items.e: It solves the cause of the problem while protecting species.

items.q: Which human impact are terraces and contour plowing designed to reduce?
c: car exhaust releasing carbon monoxide and smog gases
soil washing off steep farm fields
farms wasting water through flood irrigation
items.e: Match the solution to the problem.

items.q: Why does cutting down a forest add to climate change?
c: trees produce carbon dioxide in photosynthesis
fewer trees take in CO₂, and burning or rotting wood releases stored carbon
forests block greenhouse gases from reaching space
items.e: Forests are carbon sinks; removing them turns a sink into a source.

items.q: Which human impact are cover crops and buffer strips of plants designed to reduce?
c: soil washing off steep farm fields
sulfur dioxide from coal plants causing acid rain
items.e: Match the solution to the problem.

items.q: Which is an example of adapting to climate change rather than slowing it?
c: switching from coal to wind power
building higher flood walls and planting trees for shade in cities
items.e: Mitigation reduces the cause; adaptation reduces the damage.

items.q: Lorna's class studies this problem: “An invasive vine is smothering native plants.” Which solution would best protect biodiversity?
c: remove the vine and replant native species
items.e: It solves the cause of the problem while protecting species.

items.q: Which human impact are wildlife crossings over or under roads designed to reduce?
c: farms wasting water through flood irrigation
highways cutting animals off from their habitat
dams blocking salmon from swimming upstream
items.e: Match the solution to the problem.

items.q: Miguel's class studies this problem: “A wetland was drained and nearby towns now flood.” Which solution would best protect biodiversity?
items.e: It solves the cause of the problem while protecting species.

items.q: Why does using less fertilizer protect lakes?
c: fertilizer adds too much salt to the ocean
extra nitrogen and phosphorus wash into water and cause algal blooms
items.e: When the algae die, decomposers use up the oxygen, and fish can die.

items.q: What is the Three Sisters planting method?
c: watering crops three times a day
planting three rows of the same crop
growing corn, beans and squash together so each plant helps the others
items.e: Corn supports the beans, beans add nitrogen and squash leaves shade the soil and keep moisture in.

items.q: What is a carbon sink?
c: something that takes in more carbon dioxide than it releases, such as a forest or the ocean
items.e: Oceans, soils and forests remove CO₂ from the atmosphere.

items.q: Joshua's class studies this problem: “Forest animals are trapped in small patches between farms.” Which solution would best protect biodiversity?
c: connect the patches with wildlife corridors
items.e: It solves the cause of the problem while protecting species.

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: sewage polluting rivers?
items.e: Engineers design solutions that reduce harm to natural systems.

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: landfill chemicals leaking into groundwater?
items.e: Engineers design solutions that reduce harm to natural systems.

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: oil spills from tankers?
items.e: Engineers design solutions that reduce harm to natural systems.

items.q: What is a climate change indicator?
c: a measurement that shows how the climate is changing, such as sea-ice extent or average temperature
items.e: Indicators are tracked over many years to show trends.
